response.sql: WITH dc AS (SELECT a.district_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account a JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY a.district_id, d.A3), ra AS (SELECT dc.*, AVG(account_count) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_avg FROM dc), ab AS (SELECT * FROM ra WHERE account_count > region_avg) SELECT district_id, region, account_count, account_count - region_avg AS excess_over_region_avg, account_count * 1.0 / AVG(account_count) OVER () AS ratio_to_overall_avg FROM ab ORDER BY ratio_to_overall_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The region average is taken over districts that have at least one account (districts with zero accounts are not in the per-district counts).
The final ratio divides by the average account count across all above-average districts (not just the top 10), computed before the LIMIT.
